column4: note

Bolita alone is too generic and blends into the "Bolita de X" family used for n015/n034/n079/n080; 团团 means round/plump ("Roly"), so "rollizito" (from rollizo, plump) matches the meaning and gives this creature its own identity.
Cuenta overwhelmingly means "bill/account" in everyday Spanish; "cuentita" reads as "little bill", not "little bead". "Canicita" (little marble) reads unambiguously as a small round bead-like thing.

Concha is common/neutral for "shell" in most of Latin America but is vulgar slang for female genitalia in the Río de la Plata region (Argentina/Uruguay/Paraguay) — risky for neutral pan-LatAm content. "Cascarita" (little shell/husk) sidesteps that.
Same "concha" concern as n066; paired with the fix there using the established "-ín" little-form pattern.
Plural "Olitas" reads as "waves" rather than an individual creature's name; every other entry in the set is a singular nickname (cf. Ondita right below it).

Marito isn't a real diminutive of "mar" (which takes "-cito": amor→amorcito, mar→marcito); also swaps with n071 so the set follows its own convention (reduplicated form gets the regular diminutive, "little X" form gets "-ín").
Currently duplicates the (corrected) n070 gloss. As the "little X" (小海) entry it should take the "-ín" pattern used elsewhere (Piedrín, Frijolín, Lunín), giving "Marín" and avoiding the collision.
Missing the required dieresis: "agua" → "agüita" (the ü keeps the /gw/ sound before i). "Aguita" as written is a common but incorrect spelling.

Goterita evokes "gotera" (a leak/drip stain, e.g. a roof leak), not a small drop. The plain diminutive of "gota" is "gotita", but that's already used for n089 (雨滴/Raindrop); "gotín" keeps the correct root while avoiding the collision.

Helado means "ice cream" as a noun in everyday LatAm Spanish, so "Heladito" reads as "little ice cream", not "icy". "Hielito" (from hielo, ice) is unambiguous, and also restores the set's own pattern (reduplicated 冰冰 form gets the regular diminutive).
Currently duplicates the (corrected) n081 gloss. As the "little X" (小冰) entry it should take the "-ín" pattern, giving "Hielín" and avoiding the collision with n081.
Esponjita evokes a bath/kitchen sponge, not "fluffy". "Pelusita" (little fuzz/fluff, from pelusa) matches the texture meant by 朵朵/"Fluffy" and doesn't collide with n094's "Algodoncito".

Plata very commonly means "money" in colloquial LatAm Spanish ("no tengo plata"), so "Platita" is likely to be read as "a little money" rather than "silvery". "Plateadito" (from plateado, silver-colored) avoids that.
Same "plata" = money concern as n085; paired fix using the set's own "-ín" pattern for the little-form.
潮 means tide, not coast; "Costerita" (from costa, coast) shifts the meaning. "Mareíta" (from marea, tide) matches "Tidey" accurately.

Ruedita means "little wheel" (an object), but 滚滚/"Rolly" is about the rolling/tumbling motion. "Rodadita" (from rodar, to roll) matches the action, and avoids colliding with n063's corrected "Rollizito" (plumpness, a different nuance of the same English "Roly"/"Rolly").
Mofletito is about chubby cheeks, not the pouting expression itself. "Pucherito" (from "hacer pucheros", the standard idiom for a child's pout) is the precise, natural match for "Pouty".

Minor same-family caution as n066/n067: "conchuela" shares the "concha" root, but it's a distinct, less common word (a small-clam/shell term) and is unlikely to trigger the Río de la Plata vulgar reading the way plain "concha" does. Leaving as is.
Estrellamar isn't the dictionary form (which is "estrella de mar", two words) but reads clearly as a star+sea portmanteau and works fine as a cute proper-name-style nickname.
Currently uses the regular-diminutive "-ita" form, but this is the "little X" (小鲸) entry, which should take the set's "-ín" pattern; swaps with n111.

Currently uses "-ín", but 鲸鲸 is the reduplicated/base form, which elsewhere gets the regular diminutive matching the noun's gender (ballena is feminine → Ballenita); swaps with n110, also removing the duplicate-gloss collision between the two.
